import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Wieferich primes

A Wieferich prime is a prime number $p$ such that $p^2$ divides $2^{p-1} - 1$. By Fermat's
little theorem every odd prime $p$ divides $2^{p-1} - 1$, so Wieferich primes are those for
which this divisibility holds to the second power. The only known Wieferich primes are $1093$
and $3511$. It is conjectured that there are infinitely many Wieferich primes.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Wieferich prime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wieferich_prime)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [OEIS A001220](https://oeis.org/A001220)
-/

namespace WieferichPrime2

/--
Are there infinitely many Wieferich primes?

A Wieferich prime is a prime $p$ such that $p^2 \mid 2^{p-1} - 1$. The conjectured answer is
affirmative: it is conjectured that infinitely many Wieferich primes exist.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem wieferich_prime_2 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ^ 2 ∣ 2 ^ (p - 1) - 1}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- The prime $1093$ is a Wieferich prime. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem wieferich_1093 : Nat.Prime 1093 ∧ 1093 ^ 2 ∣ 2 ^ (1093 - 1) - 1 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, ?_⟩
  decide +kernel

/-- The prime $3511$ is a Wieferich prime. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem wieferich_3511 : Nat.Prime 3511 ∧ 3511 ^ 2 ∣ 2 ^ (3511 - 1) - 1 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, ?_⟩
  decide +kernel

/-- The prime $2$ is not a Wieferich prime: $4 \nmid 2^1 - 1 = 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_wieferich_two : ¬ (Nat.Prime 2 ∧ 2 ^ 2 ∣ 2 ^ (2 - 1) - 1) := by
  decide

/-- The prime $3$ is not a Wieferich prime: $9 \nmid 2^2 - 1 = 3$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_wieferich_three : ¬ (Nat.Prime 3 ∧ 3 ^ 2 ∣ 2 ^ (3 - 1) - 1) := by
  decide

end WieferichPrime2

/-!
# Wieferich primes

A Wieferich prime is a prime $p$ such that $p^2$ divides $2^{p-1} - 1$. The only known
examples are $1093$ and $3511$, and any further Wieferich prime exceeds $2^{64}$. It is
conjectured that infinitely many Wieferich primes exist.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Wieferich prime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wieferich_prime)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [OEIS A001220](https://oeis.org/A001220)
-/

namespace WieferichPrime2

/-- A Wieferich prime is a prime $p$ such that $p^2 \mid 2^{p-1} - 1$. -/
def IsWieferichPrime (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  p.Prime ∧ p ^ 2 ∣ 2 ^ (p - 1) - 1

/-- Are there infinitely many Wieferich primes? The conjectured answer is yes: there are
infinitely many primes $p$ with $p^2 \mid 2^{p-1} - 1$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem wieferich_prime_2 : {p : ℕ | IsWieferichPrime p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- The prime $1093$ is a Wieferich prime. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem isWieferichPrime_1093 : IsWieferichPrime 1093 := by
  set_option exponentiation.threshold 4000 in
  norm_num [IsWieferichPrime]

/-- The prime $3511$ is a Wieferich prime. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem isWieferichPrime_3511 : IsWieferichPrime 3511 := by
  set_option exponentiation.threshold 4000 in
  norm_num [IsWieferichPrime]

/-- The prime $2$ is not a Wieferich prime, since $4 \nmid 2^1 - 1 = 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_isWieferichPrime_two : ¬ IsWieferichPrime 2 := by
  norm_num [IsWieferichPrime]

/-- The prime $3$ is not a Wieferich prime, since $9 \nmid 2^2 - 1 = 3$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_isWieferichPrime_three : ¬ IsWieferichPrime 3 := by
  norm_num [IsWieferichPrime]

/-- The primality condition excludes $0$ and $1$, which satisfy the divisibility condition
alone (in `ℕ`, `0 ^ 2 ∣ 2 ^ (0 - 1) - 1` reduces to `0 ∣ 0`). -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_isWieferichPrime_zero_one : ¬ IsWieferichPrime 0 ∧ ¬ IsWieferichPrime 1 := by
  norm_num [IsWieferichPrime]

end WieferichPrime2

* [Wikipedia, Wieferich prime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wieferich_prime)

  ⟨by norm_num, by decide +kernel⟩
